title: Phin is a win! Full flavor strong coffee!
text:
Ive purchased the standard and large, both are working incredibly well. I watched a few videos on YouTube to understand it. The phin requires a bit of practice to get it right, once you do, you're in for an amazing cup of coffee. Full of flavor, as strong as you like with little to no grounds if done correctly.

I use the standard size to make myself a nice large cup of coffee. I use 14-17 grams of coffee. I grind just a bit more course than medium. It's a 15 on my heihox hand grinder. I presoak and fill the standard all the way. This produces a very small amount of very strong coffee. I add some condensed milk and add hot water until my 14oz mug is full. I'm likely adding 7-8 oz of water and I still get a very strong cup. I find it too strong without being poured over ice or a significant amount of water, but that's just me, you may love it full strength.

I tried using the Trung Nguyen brand but that seemed to be too finely ground, after 4 tries I gave up and went back to freshly grinding at 15 with my heihox. Keeping in mind the grind size of Trung Nguyen, this should give you an idea about where I grind. My grinder would be at a 9-11 grinding equivalent to Trung Nguyen, and I need a 15 for my phin to work perfect for me. Grind size is very important to make sure you get a strong cup that's still warm.

Grind too fine and it'll stall and take way to long to finish and the cup will be cold. I'm normally seeing between 4-6 min for a brew, I fill all the way to the top on the standard and large.

I really enjoy the coffee I get from the phin, it's strong and full of flavor. I find less sediment using a phin compared to a French press. This is not going to produce as clean of a cup as a paper filtered pour-over, but I find it cleaner than a french press.

Overall, I highly recommend the phin. It's takes some practice to get a perfect technique, and that's half the fun for me. I can greatly vary the strength, clean it easily and it requires no paper filters. The phin is a win, win, win!

I'm very impressed with the quality of this sieve. It separates out the very fine particles (think Turkish grind fine). I have noticed a definite improvement in the taste of my coffee by removing these fines. However, be aware it will also make your coffee taste weaker unless you add the beans to compensate for what you are removing.

Some considerations:

It's pretty small. I typically just brew 6 cups for myself and my spouse using 1.1 oz of beans. This fits just fine with plenty of room to shake. 2.2 oz of beans to do a whole pot probably won't fit well though (I haven't tried yet to be sure). I'm pretty sure most folks use more beans than I do as well. I generally lose 10% by weight to fines, whether I use my own burr grinder or commercially ground coffee by a local business.

It takes time. This is a very fine sieve, and I end up shaking it for a few minutes to be satisfied I've gotten out enough fines.

The fines stick to the sieve somewhat. I tap it pretty thoroughly on the counter to bang them down before opening, and then further tap the sieve inside and against the base, but invariably there ends up being some mess from coffee fines coming out.

Overall: satisfied. It meets our needs.

title: making tea in a nalgene
text:
I like making A LOT of tea at once, and it's super convenient to make it in a nalgene bottle--it's okay with hot water, easy to clean, easy to take with me, makes a WONDERFUL hot water bottle until it's drinkable. Usually I just use bagged tea, but I really want something that will let me make fancy tea in my decidedly unfancy container. So I recognize that I'm already outside of the targeted design for this thing, and it's just my first time using it, but there are already a couple of things I noticed:

The bottom silicon bit doesn't have any sort of drain holes. I suppose maybe they'd be too big and let grounds out in the case of coffee making? but it means the base stays filled with liquid even after you pull it out of the container. Probably just annoying when you're making cold brew coffee, excitingly dangerous with the tea. There are certainly design alternatives they could have gone with for that, good luck not making a mess any temperature you use it at.

The lid is small enough to fit into a nalgene bottle comfortably, but JUST. So pulling it back out is a bit of an adventure. you also have to push it all the way into the container to pour water over it (again, presumably less hazardous when it's not boiling water, bit of an adventure when it was.). bottom has a bit of little feet on the side that make it almost as big as the top, so pulling it out of the nalgene was also a bit scary like "am I pulling too hard, will this thing fall apart midprocess and make me really sad?" and so far (2x) it hasn't, but you're still going to want to be careful about taking it out of the tube.

what i'd like to see if this was really designed for tea (or hot coffee I guess): a lip on the lid to allow it to hang from the top of the bottle instead of having to be stuck in there, drainage through the bottom. But it's the first thing I've found that's actually sized well enough to go into the nalgene in the first place, so it's a start at least!

(Also, i'm not a coffee drinker, but given that the base is hollow and apparently can be pushed up inside the tube for shorter bottles than mine (32 oz nalgene big mouth), the fact that it has measurements on the outside is confusing (because the amount the inside holds will depend on the height of the assembled tube?) , so probably people should not follow those especially at first.)

Unlike others, I don't mind not knowing the sieve size. It's the taste that matters and that is improved. There is a slight but noticeable improvement in the taste of the coffee; somewhat smoother. A gentle tap on the counter helps free up most of the powder but there is still an annoying amount that gets out to the counter, your hands, and the immediate surroundings. title: Good idea, well made product, but some shortcomings for me.  Not the right tool for the (my) job.
text:
After seeing a couple of videos on YouTube I decided to track this sifter down and give it a shot for the reasons it was promoted for, removing tiny 'fines' that cause bitterness and sludge in my coffee. FYI, I'm using a French press. I gave it a few months of trial and error before deciding to post my two cents...

I think it's designed and made well, so no issues there, and no issues in shipping that some folks seem to ding products in reviews for.

For me the shortcomings boil down to two things that affected my personal experience:

The overall size is just too small. Others here have mentioned this as well from an overall quantity perspective... It's clearly a single serving size, which is actually all I need, so that wasn't my issue. Larger would obviously be more versatile, but for me, I would have liked larger to get a more aggressive shake AND more mesh surface area for the small particles to sift through. I think this would improve the results of the sifting process. I found that the mesh holes clogged up pretty quickly with particles that tried to fit through the mesh, but got stuck. The extra surface area would help with that. FWIW, it's very easy to clean the stuck particles by wiping over the outer surface of the mesh with you hand and simply tapping it on a hard surface.

The other shortcoming for me is that the mesh is simply too fine. It does sift out very fine powder as it is designed to do, but after doing some experimentation with a few other sifting processes, I found that many of the particles that this didn't sift out were still contributing to some bitterness and sludge. I personally found that I want to sift out some slightly larger particles. In other words, this did about half the job I wanted it to do. Your experience may be different...

To summarize, close but no cigar for me. It does something, but not quite enough. One of the reasons I tried this out is the very affordable cost. In the end, I'm going to spend more money than I really wanted to, but will ultimately get what I'm going for out of my cup of coffee. I won't promote specific other products here out of respect for this vendor, but the solution to my specific concerns is out there, it just costs a lot more!
